children: Rigetti Computing announced two related agreements with the U.S. Department of Commerce to advance superconducting quantum computing. The company entered an Other Transaction Agreement for up to $100 million in CHIPS Act funding, including a $43.9 million initial disbursement and two milestone-based tranches of $29.9 million and $26.2 million. In a linked step, Rigetti will issue 7,739,938 common shares at an implied $12.92 per share, totaling $100 million, to the Department, with transfer limits, registration rights, and voting restrictions. The funding targets miniaturized readout electronics, a next-generation cryostat, and high-connectivity chip fabrication, with a performance period of up to five years.
